_note: Synthetic-but-labeled reference dataset used as a 'population prior' for cold-start suggestions. These are illustrative figures inspired by general behavioral-psych findings on regret (e.g. omission vs. commission regret, decision fatigue, social/rest tradeoffs) -- they are NOT drawn from a real personal dataset and must always be surfaced to users as general patterns, never as personalized predictions. high_regret_advice/low_regret_advice are only set on specific (tagged) categories -- the general catch-all categories are too broad to safely auto-resolve. planning_alignment (+1/-1/null) marks whether the measured action is the spontaneous-leaning choice (+1, e.g. skipping/canceling/avoiding) or the planner-leaning choice (-1, e.g. saving/following through) -- used to nudge the prior toward a user's onboarding-survey planning style before personal data exists. null on general catch-all categories: too broad to safely nudge either way.

entries.description: People who skip sleep for social plans or late obligations report regret about 65% of the time.
People who skip a planned workout report regret about 58% of the time.
People who skip a meal when hungry report regret about 71% of the time.
Across health-related routine decisions, people report regret about 55% of the time when they deviate from their usual habit.
People who cancel social plans last minute report regret about 45% of the time.
People who go out despite feeling low-energy report regret about 38% of the time -- lower than expected, since going tends to be regretted less than skipping.
entries.low_regret_advice: go, you'll probably be glad you did

entries.description: Across social decisions in general, people report regret about 42% of the time.
People who make impulse purchases report regret about 62% of the time.
People who choose to save or invest instead of spending report regret about 22% of the time.
entries.high_regret_advice: spend it if you need to

entries.description: Across financial decisions in general, people report regret about 40% of the time.
People who avoid a difficult conversation report regret about 55% of the time.
entries.low_regret_advice: it's fine to let it go

entries.description: People who reach out first after a disagreement or silence report regret about 20% of the time.
Across interpersonal decisions in general, people report regret about 45% of the time.
Across everyday routine decisions, people report regret about 35% of the time.
